newsitem.title: UK: India's car market to overtake China - US analyst.
newsitem.headline: India's car market to overtake China - US analyst.

text.p: The Indian car market is likely to enjoy a sales boom before China does, thanks to India's more developed consumer demand, leading U.S. motor industry analyst J.D. Power & Associates said here on Friday.

At an international conference on the global outlook for the industry, Brian Heywood, its Asian expert, told delegates: "Consumers will drive the sales growth in Asia. But I think China will not see a major consumer market in the next five years (under existing conditions). It will take up to seven years, whereas India will take off in three to five."

"Too much focus is placed on the Chinese market alone," said Heywood in a presentation on growth prospects in Asia. He said despite its size advantage, volume of sales to consumers were behind those to government departments and officials and others.
The true growth would come from the consumer, said J D Power's analyst concluding that in the medium term India remained a more attractive place for car manufacturers.
He said within a market of three billion people, Asia excluding Japan had only one car per 700-800 people, compared to one in 13 in the U.S., one in 17 in Japan and one in 30 in Western Europe.
